root_cause.symptom: OPEN_EVENT_CALENDAR_DETAIL failed 46 times (23 in the last 2 days); every failure is EVENT_CALENDAR_DETAIL_NOT_PROVEN with an identity mismatch.
root_cause.probe_result: This probe reproduced the whole production path and ALL FOUR verifier conditions PASSED (first_failing_condition=None): readers and verifier are not broken.
root_cause.why_the_probe_passed_but_production_fail: Today's first grid entry (除雪小分队, 1C9F9BD8F5) is OPEN, so its detail page prints a preview window (2026-10-13 00:00 - 2026-10-15 24:00) and the calendar title was read in full, so the exact-event-id path matched. Production picks the first STORE-uninspected entry, which is usually a NOT-YET-OPEN event - exactly the case whose attribution cannot succeed.
chain: 1. The resolver taps event_schedule.calendar_next_entry() = the first entry the STORE says is uninspected. Uninspected entries are mostly future events (open ones get inspected and stop being the next one).

2. For a not-yet-open event the detail page prints no preview window, so match_calendar_detail_to_entry() bails at the start/end None check -> returns None -> attributed_event_id stays empty (observed empty in all sampled failures).

3. The exact-id path cannot rescue it because _event_id() is sha1(OCR title)[:10] for unregistered events, and the calendar-side title is frequently a PARTIAL read: the failing frame shows the same real event as 除雪 (DC53E03FB8) on the calendar and 除雪小分队 (1C9F9BD8F5) on the detail -> two different ids for one event.

4. next_detail_event_id is never written anywhere in the codebase (only read by the verifier), so the verifier's expectation always falls back to the first entry with tap_norm and details_observed not True, taken from the before-frame calendar.
root_cause.secondary_defect_seen_in_the_same_frame: The 2026-10-10 grid listed DISCOVERED_EVENT_6F33C054CA (英雄集结) TWICE with different date ranges (10/08..10/11 and 10/12..10/14) - one event_id for two occurrences. occurrence_key exists for this, but any consumer keyed on event_id alone will conflate them.
root_cause.fix_direction: Do not gate attribution on the presence of a preview window: an unambiguous unique name match should be attributable on its own, and the not-yet-open case is precisely the one that needs it. Keep the date-overlap check as a tie-breaker/confirmation, not as a precondition. Separately, identity must not rest on a partial OCR string - either read the full bar text on the calendar side or reconcile by prefix/subset before hashing.
evidence: offline re-read of that episode's before/after frames (entries + tap_norm)
winter_agent_v2/event_calendar.py: _event_id (sha1 of the label), match_calendar_detail_to_entry (date-overlap precondition), runtime.py:5121 EVENT_CALENDAR_NEXT_DETAIL resolver

correction_2026_10_13_late.what_was_wrong: The root_cause block concluded on 2026-10-13 afternoon was INCOMPLETE and its fix direction was wrong. It was written without reading .workbuddy-ai/handoff/THE_CALENDAR_DETAIL_LOOP_ASKS_A_QUESTION_ALREADY_ANSWERED_20261010.md, which already documents the same failure signature, the same id-drift pairs, AND two implemented fixes.
correction_2026_10_13_late.what_was_right: The probe's own measurement still stands: the production path reproduced end to end and all four verifier conditions passed (first_failing_condition=None), i.e. the readers/verifier are not broken and the blocker is attribution/identity. The observed evidence (expected DC53E03FB8 vs actual 1C9F9BD8F5, attribution empty) is exactly the signature that document records.
correction_2026_10_13_late.what_was_missed: The fix is not 'relax the date gate and wire the fuzzy name matcher'. That matcher (match_calendar_detail_to_entry) is dead code, and the project deliberately rejected a too-wide fallback once already (its own A/B caught it). The implemented approach lives on the branch codex/production-pin-recovery and is: (1) f9b6ee60 credit a detail by its own dates when OCR changed the identifier, (2) 8eb16ff7 recognise the preview card a grid tap opens, and (3) af4c1186 attribute the opened card to the row the run actually aimed at -- which is precisely the 'next step' the 2026-10-10 document listed as unimplemented. abe67449 then records the loop as closed, measured in the ledger.
correction_2026_10_13_late.code_change_reverted: Two source files (winter_agent_v2/event_calendar.py, winter_agent_v2/runtime.py) were edited to relax the date gate and wire the fuzzy matcher. Both edits were REVERTED with explicit-path git checkout after the handoff was read. The probe tool and this evidence file are kept.
correction_2026_10_13_late.the_real_finding: The two trees have diverged: codex/production-pin-recovery (HEAD 2b85647a, 647 dirty paths) is ~50 commits ahead of main (merge-base 25810c7f), and main's only unique commits are this session's three (e91ac4a3, cb825d74, 51d536c9). The truth audit already flagged this as version_active CONFLICT: 2b85647 vs HEAD=25810c7f. So the calendar fix exists in production but NOT on main -- which is why reading main's source made the fix look absent.
correction_2026_10_13_late.verification_of_the_pin_fix: tests/test_calendar_detail_attribution.py + tests/test_event_calendar.py in the pin worktree: 44 passed (pytest printed [100%]; the summary line is lost to this machine's known pytest teardown hang, documented in docs/GITHUB_SYNC_RULES.md).
correction_2026_10_13_late.lesson: A defect that looks live may already be fixed on another branch. Before designing a fix, read the dated handoff notes AND check whether the branch you are reading is the one that carries production. The function being dead code was true of main and irrelevant to production.
